tldr: By combining a denoising model that estimates environmental and privileged information solely from proprioception (joint angles and IMU) without exteroceptive sensors like cameras or LiDAR, together with Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP) mimicking human movement, the authors propose a reinforcement learning framework that allows humanoids to traverse stairs and rough terrain smoothly and robustly.
hero_caption: Overall architecture of the DAMP framework. An LSTM encoder extracts latent variables $z_t$ from proprioceptive time series, while a decoder—used only during training—performs denoised learning by reconstructing privileged information $s_t$. The policy receives both task rewards and AMP style rewards, optimized in a single-stage end-to-end process.
overview:
Humanoid robots have the potential to overcome high steps and rough terrain thanks to their bipedal locomotion. However, with a high center of mass and many degrees of freedom, they are vulnerable to disturbances and prone to falling. In recent years, deep reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved impressive traversal performance, but relying on exteroceptive sensors such as cameras or LiDAR introduces computational overhead and sensor drift (measurement discrepancies). On the other hand, blind locomotion relying solely on joint and IMU feedback makes it extremely difficult to handle collisions with stairs or tall obstacles.

To tackle this, the authors propose DAMP (Denoised Belief Learning with Adversarial Motion Priors), a framework enabling smooth traversal over steep, challenging terrain even in a completely "blind" state without exteroceptive sensors. The core idea consists of two components. First, a belief learning mechanism that smartly reconstructs and denoises "privileged information"—such as terrain profiles and contact states—in a latent space from past temporal sensor history. Second, an AMP framework using a generative adversarial setup to imitate human walking motions, preventing awkward, unstable gaits and promoting natural, human-like walking.

For evaluation, tests were conducted both in simulation and in the real world using the 18-DoF humanoid robot "Noetix N2." DAMP significantly outperformed conventional methods, demonstrating effortless traversal over 15 cm stairs, 20 cm curbs, and cobblestone-covered rough terrain. Furthermore, it tackled the 100-meter obstacle course at the "World Humanoid Robot Games 2025," successfully completing all terrains without a single fall.
contributions: Built an LSTM-based denoising encoder-decoder structure that implicitly reconstructs privileged states from proprioceptive history without using exteroceptive sensors.
Integrated Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP) and a Lipschitz continuity penalty (LCP) to achieve both human-like smoothness and disturbance-resistant control outputs across harsh, rough terrain.
Eliminated multi-stage pipelines such as privileged-information distillation, achieving an end-to-end learning framework completed in a single stage with PPO.

Directly deployed the policy on the real humanoid robot "Noetix N2," demonstrating successful traversal of 15 cm stairs and rough terrain, as well as completing the entire 100 m obstacle course at a robotics competition.

sections.heading: Can humanoids climb stairs without exteroceptive sensors?
sections.summary: Rough-terrain locomotion for humanoids is even harder than for quadruped robots. To overcome the weaknesses of conventional sensor-dependent methods and pure RL, this paper introduces DAMP, combining denoised belief learning with human motion imitation.
sections.details:
Having humanoid robots traverse complex terrains such as stairs and rubble is substantially harder than doing so with quadruped robots. With a higher center of mass, numerous joint degrees of freedom, and complex kinematics, humanoids can easily lose balance once their footing is tripped.

Traditional model-based controls, such as ZMP (Zero Moment Point) and MPC (Model Predictive Control), rely on precise mathematical models of environmental dynamics, limiting their adaptability to highly irregular terrains. Meanwhile, model-free deep reinforcement learning (RL) adapts well to unknown environments and has advanced rapidly. However, RL policies trained strictly on reward functions often result in awkward, energy-inefficient motions, struggling to negotiate consecutive 10 cm steps or 20 cm obstacles.

Mounting cameras or LiDARs is one approach, but it comes with heavy computational costs, sensor drift, and susceptibility to occlusions. Researchers have also explored imitating human motion data (such as via AMP) to encourage natural behavior, yet merely mimicking motion lacks the robustness needed to traverse severe terrain.

This study proposes DAMP to address these issues. By using an LSTM-based encoder-decoder to implicitly infer advantageous privileged information while filtering out observation noise, and coupling it with human-like motion guidance via AMP, the system trains end-to-end in a single stage to conquer harsh terrains on the physical humanoid "Noetix N2."

sections.heading: The basics of POMDPs and adversarial imitation learning
sections.summary: Humanoid locomotion is formulated as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP). This section also reviews the fundamentals of AMP, which acquires natural motion styles through adversarial training rather than strictly tracking reference trajectories.
sections.details:
This section reviews the problem formulation and foundational techniques.

When a robot walks across unknown terrain, it cannot observe the full state of the environment. It only receives limited observations such as joint angles and IMU readings. Therefore, this study models the problem as a POMDP (Partially Observable Markov Decision Process). A recurrent neural network (RNN) is adopted for the policy $\pi$, taking past observation histories $\mathbf{o}_{1:t}$ into account to determine actions $\mathbf{a}_t$.

Furthermore, to help the robot acquire natural, human-like walking, AMP (Adversarial Motion Prior) is incorporated. Unlike traditional methods that reward how accurately reference joint trajectories are tracked, AMP leverages a GAN-style (Generative Adversarial Network) mechanism.

Specifically, a discriminator $D_\psi$ is trained to distinguish between expert walking data $\mathcal{D}_E$ and the robot's own locomotion data $\mathcal{D}_\pi$. The policy earns a higher style reward $r^s$ the better it fools the discriminator into judging its motion as natural and human-like. This avoids rigid trajectory tracking constraints, balancing task accomplishment (moving forward) with natural bodily movement.

sections.heading: The DAMP architecture: Denoising and smoothing mechanisms
sections.summary: Explains DAMP's core system architecture. The key to success lies in combining a denoising model that reconstructs privileged information, a Lipschitz continuity penalty for smooth control, and curriculum learning.
sections.details:
DAMP incorporates multiple design choices to achieve seamless Sim-to-Real transfer in a single stage of training.

### III-A Overall Architecture and Networks
The policy network consists of an LSTM encoder and an MLP actor. Its inputs are solely proprioceptive: target velocity commands, IMU angular velocities, gravity vector, joint positions and velocities, and the previous action. Meanwhile, during training only, the Critic network that evaluates the value function receives privileged information $\mathbf{s}_t$, including true linear velocities, payload weight, friction coefficients, motor strengths, foot contact states, and a $1.2\,\mathrm{m} \times 0.8\,\mathrm{m}$ surrounding height scan.

### III-B Denoising Model (DWL Module)
This is the most critical component. The LSTM encoder maps the observation history to a latent variable $\mathbf{z}_t$, while a decoder is trained to reconstruct the privileged information $\mathbf{s}_t$ from $\mathbf{z}_t$ during training. Funneling high-dimensional observations through a lower-dimensional latent space creates an information bottleneck that strips away noise. In addition, $L_1$ regularization is applied to the latent variables to encourage sparsity. During deployment on the real robot, the decoder is discarded, running only the encoder and actor. This enables control informed by hidden environmental features without any exteroceptive sensors.

### III-C Lipschitz Continuity Penalty (LCP)
In legged robots, minor fluctuations in observations that trigger sudden command torque spikes can cause falls or motor overheating. To prevent this, a Lipschitz continuity penalty is introduced to constrain the gradients of the policy network with respect to its inputs. This enforces smooth, stable control outputs, ensuring joint commands do not drastically fluctuate even when inputs waver slightly.

### III-D Training Details
Training was conducted in NVIDIA IsaacGym and completed in just 5 hours (7,000 iterations) using a single RTX 4090 GPU. Thorough domain randomization across robot parameters and environmental friction, combined with curriculum learning that gradually escalates terrain difficulty, ensured high adaptability to the physical robot.

Simultaneously, an AMP discriminator provides style rewards, with the entire system optimized collaboratively via PPO.

sections.heading: Traversing stairs and 20 cm curbs on hardware: What ablations reveal
sections.summary: Validation was conducted on the 18-DoF physical robot 'Noetix N2'. In addition to simulation ablation studies, this section reports real-world traversals over stairs and harsh terrains, as well as completing a 100 m obstacle course at a robotics competition.
sections.details:
Experiments used the humanoid robot "Noetix N2" (1.2 m tall, 33 kg, 18 degrees of freedom), running the policy at a control frequency of 50 Hz.

### IV-B Simulation Evaluation and Ablations
To identify which components drove performance, DAMP was compared against three setups: (1) removing the denoising loss, (2) removing AMP (imitation learning), and (3) the baseline HIM from prior work.
Removing denoising severely degraded terrain adaptation, showing that simply maintaining temporal memory is insufficient to infer internal states well. Removing AMP led to unnatural, asymmetrical gaits, causing increased foot collisions and vibrations. Interestingly, adding AMP also constrained the exploration space, yielding a substantial secondary benefit of speeding up training convergence.

### IV-C Real-World Locomotion Tests and Competition
In hardware tests, each method was evaluated across 20 trials on various rough terrains: 15 cm stairs, 20-degree slopes, uneven flagstone paths, 20 cm curbs, and obstacles with scattered cobblestones. DAMP achieved overwhelmingly superior success rates across all terrains, displaying remarkable recovery by quickly repositioning its footing when its feet were tripped.

The ultimate showcase was tackling the 100-meter obstacle course at the "World Humanoid Robot Games 2025." Navigating 10 official obstacle areas (A to J) via completely blind walking without any exteroceptive sensors, the robot successfully completed the full course without a single fall.

sections.heading: Conclusions and future outlook
sections.summary: Combining implicit state estimation from observations, imitation learning, and Lipschitz continuity constraints proves that highly robust humanoid locomotion can be achieved without exteroceptive sensors.
sections.details:
This paper presented DAMP, a framework that enables blind humanoid robots to walk naturally and robustly across harsh real-world terrains.

Rigorous simulation ablation experiments confirmed that both components—belief learning that estimates and denoises privileged information from past observations, and guidance from human motion priors—are essential. Furthermore, real-world hardware trials demonstrated high success rates across stairs, slopes, and irregular rubble surfaces.

Achieving such high adaptability purely through body feedback (proprioception) without relying on exteroceptive cameras or LiDAR represents a powerful approach toward stable, autonomous bipedal operation in real-world environments plagued by sensor uncertainties.

takeaways: Even without exteroceptive sensors (cameras or LiDAR), reconstructing privileged states with denoising from proprioceptive time-series allows humanoids to traverse stairs and 20 cm obstacles.
Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP) do more than just make motions look human-like; they prevent unnatural gaits and dramatically accelerate reinforcement learning convergence.
Incorporating a Lipschitz continuity penalty (LCP) into policy optimization curbs abrupt joint torque fluctuations and enhances Sim-to-Real transferability.
A high-performing policy that deploys directly to real hardware can be learned in a single-stage end-to-end framework, eliminating the need for two-stage teacher-student pipelines.
limitations: Because this is entirely 'blind walking' without exteroceptive sensors, reactions are purely reactive—sensing step height only after foot impact—making it impossible to proactively handle excessively tall steps or pitfall-like drops.
AMP training relies heavily on high-quality human motion datasets, meaning performance can be constrained by kinematic compatibility between the robot and the motion data.
Forward velocity commands were restricted to the range of 0.0 to 0.8 m/s; scalability to higher-speed running or dynamic jumping motions remains unverified.
